format:
WHERE THE DOCUMENT IS. The exact text Jeff received is in the scratchpad: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sstvae/92006b74-04c2-5210-829f-64b8a831fdbf/scratchpad/opt/ideas.md (124,068 bytes, 1337 lines, 21,899 words). It is the copy the main session published to /mnt/project-files/qrss-build/optimization-ideas.md on 2026-10-12 about 17:04Z. The writer agent's raw text, reassembled by me, is at .../scratchpad/optdoc_full.md (123,932 bytes, 1336 lines). A writer can read ideas.md directly to imitate it.

PROCESS WARNING FOR THE RETRO WRITER. The writer agent hit the output-token limit after 101,132 characters, was told to resume, and finished in a second message of 22,800 characters. The workflow's return value (and the journal's last result line) kept only that last message, which starts mid-word ('ker hint (native/gui/qrss_tx.hpp...'). The main session had to rejoin the two parts from the agent transcript (agent-a4f48c6da62b96d2f.jsonl). A retrospective of similar length should be written to a file in parts, or the caller should concatenate every text block.

HOW IT WAS MADE (workflow wf_d09d7a28-a9b, 10 agents). Five gather lenses in parallel: records, docs, receiver, transmit, live. Each could run at most three measurements of under 5 minutes, and said 'inferred' otherwise. Logs: 'gathered 104 ideas and 68 insights from 5 lenses'. A merge agent deduplicated these into 61 ideas and 25 insights, in six groups, ranked within each group by expected value (gain times likelihood, over cost). Three verifiers followed: evidence (39 keep, 22 revise, 6 missing), feasibility (39 keep, 22 revise, 5 missing) and gain realism (34 keep, 26 revise, 1 drop, 6 missing). The writer then applied these rules: drop an idea if two verifiers drop it or the evidence check finds its premise false; otherwise fold in every correction and keep the most conservative credible gain. It added R9, R10, L11, D10, D11 and D12 from the verifiers, dropped D4 and kept F4 marked 'not recommended'. That gives 66 idea entries in the document, though the chat reply said '61 checked ideas'. The writer prompt's style rules, verbatim: 'plain full sentences, no em-dashes, no arrow chains, no internal ids such as cmsg or session ids, units on every number. Lead with the answer.' Its prompt also asked for compact entries of 'about 4-7 lines', but real entries run 10 to 25 lines of nested bullets. Before publishing, the main session made four edits: the CE on-air sentence became 'It is on the air, in format v2 since 2026-10-10.'; the SSTVAE comparison became 'about 56 times the airtime for the same mode, in a signal 23 to 56 times narrower'; the L transmitter's push date became 2026-10-11; and the closing sentence now points the opt/ and lrx/ paths at /mnt/project-files/qrss-build/optimization/ (29 files, 328K of scripts and build records copied there). Delivery: a short chat reply named the best three items and gave a one-line recommendation ('I'd keep L on the air. Its format tweaks are worth 0.3 dB at most.'), attached the file, and posted a decision card, 'Build the band-edge noise fix and the sideband gating fix first?', with options Both fixes / L lead-in first / Measure L first / Nothing now. Jeff chose 'Both fixes' after a mis-tap, and the fixes were built and pushed as c131551 within about 2 h.

JEFF'S REQUEST FOR THE RETRO, verbatim (2026-10-13 05:24:10Z): 'Once you complete Stage 4 and are at the end of this implementation -- as I have earlier, I would love for you to express your insights about how things could be better and how we can make optimizations that might be useful. Might as well plan for this right now.' The original question (2026-10-12 14:51Z) was: 'Any additional insights gained in building Waveform L / things you noticed that we might be able to optimize in either waveform?' A memory rule also applies: 'Shareable pages open with what QRSSTVAE is vs SSTVAE.'

OUTLINE (line numbers in ideas.md):
1 '# QRSSTVAE: optimization ideas from building waveform L'
3 the date alone on its line: '2026-10-12'
5-12 '**Short answer.** Yes. Building L found these:' then four bullets, each opening with a bold one-phrase claim followed by one plain sentence: '**A measured fault in both waveforms.** ... SNR is up to 8.4 dB too high.' / '**A cheap way to find L sooner during a pass.** ... about 5 dB easier to find' / '**A finished CE feature the listener never calls.**' / '**Wasted time in the live listener.**'. Then one caveat paragraph: the deep L figures are unchecked models, and the expensive L work should wait for two offline measurements.
14-21 Shareable context: what QRSSTVAE is (codec, 30-minute passes on the quarter hour, modes A/B/C, several stations in 2.4 kHz, multi-pass combining); two bullets, **CE** and **L**, each with width, PAPR and status; the spec's thresholds (-10.9/-14.0 dB one pass, -26.4/-29.6 dB at 16 passes, 2500 Hz noise bandwidth, model figures); and the comparison with SSTVAE (airtime ratio, width ratio, 10-30 dB further below the noise).
23 '## Top picks': a numbered list of 6. Each item is '**ID: imperative title (scope).**' with indented sub-bullets: the problem with a measured number, the gain split live vs stored, and always last a line starting 'On air:' ('no change', or that old listeners decode as before). Pick 3 also carries a caveat bullet. Then '**Build first: R1 and O2.**' with three short reason bullets (small and measured; receiver-only; fix behaviour wrong on the band today), followed by sequencing paragraphs ('Land the CPU items first...', 'After those, do F1 + L1... Then R10 and O1, with D10 and D1 running offline alongside. For CE on its own, C2 is the best-supported item.'). Last comes '**One decision comes before all of this.**': hold L off the air until the format batch is decided, or accept a version bump.
66 '## What building L taught us': 8 '###' subsections holding 28 lessons. The subsections are: Where L is limited; What the clipper and the header cost; What the receiver inherited from CE; Measurement traps; Telling the waveforms apart; The store and operations; Checked and left alone; How the build went. Each lesson is a top-level bullet whose bold text is a whole-sentence claim (for example '**L buys bandwidth, not dB, at a fixed peak.**', '**Latent SNR measured by mean squared error rewards a z that has been shrunk.**', '**Live CPU does not follow progress.**', '**Mutation testing is what made the build's tests trustworthy.**'). Indented evidence bullets follow, often with bold mini-labels ('**Live A1 limit.**', '**Fading loss.**', '**KC2G 04:15Z.**'), and cross-references to idea IDs in parentheses, e.g. '(R10)', '(O22)', '(C2)'. Negative results get their own subsection ('Checked and left alone': CE beta, Si5351 error, RRC roll-off, preamble length, callsign windows, AGC cross-modulation, and a wrong claim corrected).
231-1305: six idea sections in this fixed order: '## Receiver ideas for both waveforms' (R), '## L only' (L), '## CE only' (C), '## On-air format proposals' (F), '## Live listener and operations' (O), '## Docs and tests' (D). Each opens with one or two framing lines: 'Ordered by value. R9 and R10 were added from the verifiers' findings.'; L only: 'Two facts frame every acquisition item in this section.' plus two bold bullets; format: 'Everything here goes to the spec owner, the "Decoder SNR measurement" thread, as a proposal... Each entry says whether old listeners keep working.'; operations: 'Ordered roughly as: the lock and CPU first, then transmit operation, then correctness, then coverage and display.'; docs: 'D10, D11 and D12 were added... D4 was dropped (see the closing section).'
1306 '## How these were checked': bold-led paragraphs '**Readers.**', '**Verifiers.**' (with three bullets: Evidence, Feasibility, Gain realism), '**Rules applied.**' (the drop rule, which items were added, a bullet each for '**D4 was dropped.**' and '**F4 was kept.**'), '**Measured in this round,** each run under 5 minutes:' (bullets '**By the readers:**' and '**By the verifiers:**', each listing what was measured with its script path), '**Everything else** comes from the build records and the spec... or is marked inferred.', and a last line saying where the opt/ and lrx/ paths live.

IDEA ENTRY LAYOUT. The heading is a bold line: '**R1. Take the noise floor only from bins where the front end is flat (band edges)**', that is ID, period, imperative title, optional parenthetical qualifier. Qualifiers used: (band edges), (low priority), (parked), (pairs with F1), (live only), (station-dependent), (not recommended over F1 + L1), (lowest priority), (mostly there already), (display only), (fast path, bit-identical). IDs are stable labels by group letter and are not renumbered by rank: R1, R10, R2, R4... appear in rank order, and position is the rank. Each entry has the same italic-labelled bullets in the same order: '- *What:*', '- *Why we think so:*', '- *Gain:*', '- *Cost:*', '- *Risk / constraints:*' (in the format section, '*Risk / constraints / compatibility:*'). Exceptions: O14 uses '*What already works:*' and '*What is left:*', and D5/D6 use per-part labels '*(1) README.*', '*(2) design.md, A1.*', '*(1) Log line.*'. A short label carries its text inline. A longer one has two-space-indented sub-bullets, sometimes a third level, and multi-option ideas use (a)/(b)/(c). Bold run-in labels inside evidence are allowed ('**Blind L on noise.**', '**PEP-limited station:**'). Entries are separated by a blank line, with no horizontal rules and no tables in the whole document.

HOW MEASUREMENTS AND ESTIMATES ARE SHOWN. Every number has units (dB, Hz, s, ms, %, Hz/min, 'T' for symbol periods). Every gain says whether it is measured, computed or inferred: '(measured)', '(inferred)', '(computed)', '(measured, with a clean tone)', 'Inferred and unmeasured:', 'measured this round', 'measured on synthetic LLRs'. Gains are split live vs stored passes, single pass vs 16 passes, and steady vs fading. Detection results are counts: '10 of 10 trials at -30 dB and 0 of 5 at -32 dB', '8 of 8', 'with 20 seeds per SNR'. Comparisons use 'X against Y' and 'from X to Y', never arrows. Ranges read 'about 0.1 to 0.5 dB'. Evidence cites code as file:line in plain text (frontend.py:301-347, live.py:106-108, native/gui/qrss_tx.cpp:33-34), records by file and line or section ('wfB_parts.txt:109', 'spec 5.1', 'spec line 384', 'README.md:866-869', 'e2e-results.md') and measurement scripts in parentheses ('(opt/rxcode/m3_edge_cpu.py)'). The most conservative credible gain is kept, and contrary evidence is stated ('Against the idea: spec 10 ... tells senders to change frequency on every pass'). Each Risk block says whether CE output changes ('CE needs a flag', 'CE unchanged', 'CE stays bit-identical') and, for on-air ideas, whether fielded listeners and the C beacon keep working and whether the spec owner is needed. Cost is in plain effort words (Trivial, Small, Moderate, Medium, Large, 'weeks'), often with a line count ('20 to 40 lines', 'About 80 to 150 lines of C') and the CPU cost per slot.

LENGTH AND BALANCE. 66 entries: R 10, L 11, C 4, F 8, O 22, D 11. Top picks 6, lessons 28. About 22,000 words. Jeff liked it at this length.

FULL IDEA LIST (rank order within each group; claim in brief; [port status] where the port or later work changed it):
Receiver, both waveforms:
R1 Noise floor only from bins where the front end is flat: SNR reads up to 8.4 dB high near 300/2700 Hz; 6.5 dB latent SNR lost in one joint case. [DONE pre-port as D43, c131551; ported]
R10 Re-receive stored passes once the store supplies their header: round B is worth 0.1-0.5 dB per deep L pass (0.8-1.8 dB at -12/-6 dB); the code exists and the listener never calls it. [OPEN; EM now in C++, 2-5x faster]
R2 Report and hint frequency from a line through the whole path: the spline end is 0.23-1.09 Hz off in simulation and 0.62 Hz on KC2G; the line is within 0.03 Hz.
R4 Exclude each neighbour by its own waveform's band, never fall back onto a neighbour: 0 today, about 1-3 dB of floor bias in a band packed at 30 Hz (inferred).
R3 Remember stations' frequencies as A2-only hints: about +5 dB for live L tiles of repeat stations, 1.5-2 dB for stored passes (inferred).
R9 At the finish, keep hints that fail A2 out of the gate queue: stops moved senders' due hints spending the 180 s budget (inferred). [budget arithmetic changed by C++ gate V speed]
R7 Header decoder list 8 to 32: +0.3 dB header threshold on steady paths (measured, synthetic LLRs), 1.4x decode time, about 4x false accepts; spec owner.
R6 Weight soft-header sums by each pass's consistency: under 0.1 dB (inferred).
R5 Make the inverse AGC blind to one strong L signal (low priority): about 0 at operating thresholds; cross-modulation 3.95-20.4% rms measured.
R8 Cancel the transmitter's own deterministic distortion on strong passes (parked): about 0.1 dB at the good level, 0 from two passes on.
L only:
L1 L-only A1 window over a lead-in (pairs with F1): A1 about 5 dB deeper (measured, clean tone); live L reach about -26 to about -32 dB; stored 1.5-2 dB. [OPEN]
L2 L known-waveform template search and retro detection: per-pass floor about -31 to about -36/-37 dB quiet (inferred); weeks of work. [OPEN; CE version now in C++]
L5 EM for L, starting with a header-known re-track: 0.1-0.5 dB per header-less L pass; data prior at most +0.38 dB. [OPEN; C++ rereceive skips L as Python does]
L3 L-matched A3 emission: about 2-2.5 dB on white noise (inferred).
L11 Loosen A3's threshold for L-shaped hits only: about 0.5-1 dB of blind reach (inferred).
